questionText:

"Saddle querns are found in considerable numbers at Harappan sites, and they seem to have been the only means in use for grinding cereals. As a rule, they were roughly made of hard, gritty, igneous rock or sandstone and mostly show signs of hard usage. As their bases are usually convex, they must have been set in the earth or in mud to prevent their rocking. Two main types have been found: those on which another smaller stone was pushed or rolled to and fro, and others with which a second stone was used as a pounder, eventually making a large cavity in the nether stone. Querns of the former type were probably used solely for grain; the second type were possibly used only for pounding herbs and spices for making curries. questionText: [Set 47.12] The 'Great Bath' discovered at Mohenjo-daro was a large rectangular tank situated in a courtyard. A key architectural and waterproofing feature of the Great Bath was:

options.text: Constructing the entire tank out of imported white Carrara marble
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Inverts the governing property or boundary condition.

options.text: Connecting the tank directly to the Arabian Sea via an underwater aqueduct
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Applies an adjacent or reciprocal mathematical relation.

options.text: Decorating the walls with royal dynastic relief inscriptions
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses related NCERT concepts or attributes.

options.text: Lining the brick edges with gypsum mortar and using bitumen to make the tank watertight
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Accurately solves the problem for Harappan Town Planning and Great Bath.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
For Harappan Town Planning and Great Bath (Harappan Civilisation and Archaeology (Bricks, Beads and Bones)):
Detailed Solution:
According to NCERT Class 12 History (Bricks, Beads and Bones - Harappan Town Planning and Great Bath):
The Great Bath on the Citadel of Mohenjo-daro had steps leading down on north and south sides. It was made watertight by setting bricks on edge and using a mortar of gypsum, with rooms on three sides and a well in one room.

Hence, Option (B) is the correct answer.

Therefore, option (D) is the correct answer.
